description:
Goal

A demanded TransportShape(position) refines exact semantic structure into a physical representation, while first-class callable invocation remains the intentional dynamic any boundary. ABI, backend, interpreter, and native consumers use those owned answers directly; no layer reconstructs identity from Ty, ShapeId, debug text, broad summaries, or session inventories.

Signal

- The original enum-reduce fixture compiles warning-free with materially fewer products/events and no telemetry-only allocation.
- Ordinary transport positions and callable construction owners are revision-exact, position-owned, replacement-safe, and free of legacy closure/component inventories.
- Every returning first-class callable wrapper publishes exactly one ValueRef; absent returns publish no value lane; all-divergent wrappers diverge.
- Enum, capture, suspend, and connected multi-producer fixtures cross the public callable seam uniformly, then adapt to caller-local typed destinations.
- Forward/reverse service, equal reproduction, withdrawal, and unrelated-reader coldness agree.
- Full library tests, strict clippy, formatting, targeted interpreter/JIT fixtures, and release telemetry/performance gates pass.

North-star constraints

- One requested product reads exact current fact/product authorities or returns exact waits. There is no seal, pass, whole-world census, session scan, no-change signal, or downstream reconstruction.
- Only actual product back-edges form a local settlement group, and only settled immutable answers publish.
- Physical ids are values, never semantic owners. Exact TransportPosition owners survive until physical interning.
- A dynamic boundary deliberately boxes; it must not pretend that private typed producer or caller layouts are its public ABI.
- No copied Ty/demand/provenance snapshot, reverse index, summary rescan, selector, fallback, or adapter compensation may replace discarded authority.
- Telemetry emitters pass borrowed raw authorities and minimal scalars; handlers alone inspect, transform, or retain.

Established lower model

fz-k22.5.1 supplies immutable revisioned products, exact durable dependencies, final movement states, replaceable per-publisher contributions, exact incoming-input relations, and targeted retraction.

The spike proved the lower model for ordinary positions: ExecutableInput owns its ABI from settled ActivationInputs plus RuntimeDemand; CallArg conforms to the selected input; ExecutableFacts owns normalized local structure without copied Ty/demand/layout data; TransportShape and CallableConstruction are separate position-owned domains; exact recursive shape and pass-through owner back-edges settle atomically; callable/boundary facts embed through ABI/backend values instead of physical-id inventories.

The legacy closure/component solver, demanded-id stores, global callable/boundary products, selector/fallback paths, manufactured demand, consult/freshness ledgers, and obsolete resource/representation tests are deletion targets.

Proven return-boundary correction

The demand and provenance hypotheses were falsified. Target return demand was already present in the discordant enum traces. Pairing invocation endpoints with targets can preserve correlation, but that relation is unnecessary once the public ABI is modeled correctly and would be unused provenance.

At base 140d01118 the intended contract is already explicit:

- CallableDemand is resolved surfaces, exact targets, opaque, and escape. CallableFlowEdge has no return authority.
- BackendConstructionWrapper owns one BackendCallableReturn: Diverges, Absent, or ValueRef.
- Any non-absent target result is materialized from its private raw/tuple layout to exactly one ValueRef at callable_wrapper_return_continuation.
- .agent/docs/any-value.md defines this rule: typed lanes box where they meet an any boundary.
- compiler2_native_program_jit_adapts_callable_raw_returns_back_to_value_refs executes and names the contract.

The dirty branch introduced the problem by removing BackendCallableReturn and wrapper.return_form, adding per-member boundary_return, and changing the wrapper adapter from target-to-ValueRef into target-to-caller-layout. It then introduced CallableInvocationReturn, CallableReturnAuthority, and exact_boundary_returns to choose among the conflicting caller layouts. The enum three-to-two adapter test and three-lane public tuple assertions pin this new incompatible concept, not established behavior.

The true connected fixture proves why precise caller ownership cannot work:

    fn main(flag) do
      p = fn (x) -> {:p, x} end
      r = fn (x) -> {:r, x} end
      q = fn (x) -> x end
      left = if flag, do: p, else: r
      a = left.(1)
      right = if flag, do: p, else: q
      b = right.(2)
      {a, b, p}
    end

Exact flow is P to A+B, R to A, Q to B. P, R, and Q have different private return layouts and A/B have different typed destination layouts. One boxed P value cannot publish two wrapper signatures. Under the established any boundary every non-absent wrapper returns one ValueRef, so the conflict disappears by construction and each caller continuation performs its local conversion.

Implementation strategy

1. Restore the simple CallableDemand/CallableFlow model and remove CallableUse, invocation endpoint/target/destination types, producer-publication markers, and CallableReturnAuthority.
2. Restore BackendCallableReturn and wrapper.return_form. Preserve the separately justified task_halt_repr used by zero-argument spawned tasks.
3. Delete exact_boundary_returns, PublishedReturn, BoundaryDescr return-layout/lane fields, per-member boundary_return, and precise wrapper decode/re-encode adapters. Do not restore the old boundary return-shape selector; exact flow edges already own resolution identity.
4. Make public callable return flow expose no lane for an absent result and one ValueRef for any present result. Callsite/private typed payload layouts remain downstream destinations, not public wrapper authorities.
5. Replace the branch-created exact-lane tests with production-path intent tests: uniform wrapper/source ValueRef, target-to-ValueRef materialization, caller continuation adaptation, connected graph behavior, interpreter/JIT outputs, and task halt preservation.
6. Finish the position-owned cutover, embed owner values in artifacts, delete legacy inventories/solvers/tests, update northstar and agent docs, remove every spike/probe, then run all correctness and telemetry/performance gates.

Rejected

- a callable-return ABI SCC;
- selecting a caller layout;
- choosing one producer layout;
- preserving endpoint provenance solely to repair the rejected precise-return model;
- restoring the old closure solver or return-shape selector;
- making a dynamic callable seam expose private tuple/raw lanes.

fz-k22.30 remains blocked until this lands. fz-k22.31 owns only a genuinely uncalled first-class discrepancy if one remains after the cutover.
title: Make transport shape a product-owned refinement
